benchmark_name: Wavelet Scattering Transform for Interpretable Schizophrenia Biomarker Discovery and Classification from Resting-State EEG
institutions: Department of EECE, Military Institute of Science and Technology (MIST), Mirpur Cantonment, Dhaka, Bangladesh
ground_truth_source: Publicly available Kaggle dataset of adolescents screened by psychiatrist: 39 healthy controls and 45 with schizophrenia symptoms (16-channel resting-state EEG, 128 Hz sampling rate)
size_of_benchmark: 84 subjects (4,650 retained epochs after artifact rejection); 352 scattering coefficients per epoch across 16 channels
what_assessed_skills: EEG-based schizophrenia classification; biomarker discovery via multi-scale amplitude modulation and cross-frequency coupling features; spatial interpretability of discriminative EEG features
tasks_assessed: Binary classification (schizophrenia vs. healthy control) from resting-state EEG; biomarker identification using subject-level ANOVA with FDR correction; SHAP-based feature attribution and explainability
evaluation_method: Automated evaluation; Leave-One-Subject-Out (LOSO) cross-validation (84 folds) with subject-level majority voting; metrics: Accuracy, Balanced Accuracy, Sensitivity, Specificity, F1-score, AUC-ROC, Cohen's κ, MCC. No LLMs used — classifiers are Random Forest and SVM (RBF).
llms_evaluated: None — study uses traditional ML classifiers (Random Forest, SVM with RBF kernel), not LLMs
performance_scores: Random Forest: Accuracy=90.48% (CI: 83.33–96.43%), Balanced Accuracy=90.09%, Sensitivity=95.56%, Specificity=84.62%, F1=91.49%, AUC-ROC=0.9339, Cohen's κ=0.8072, MCC=0.8110. SVM (RBF): Accuracy=79.76%, Sensitivity=82.22%, Specificity=76.92%, F1=81.32%, AUC-ROC=0.8860.
short_summary: This paper proposes a Wavelet Scattering Transform (WST) framework for interpretable schizophrenia classification and biomarker discovery from resting-state EEG. It addresses limitations of prior work (epoch-level cross-validation, static spectral features) by using multi-order WST coefficients to capture amplitude modulation and cross-frequency coupling, evaluated under strict Leave-One-Subject-Out cross-validation. Two traditional ML classifiers (Random Forest and SVM) were trained and evaluated on a public Kaggle EEG dataset of 84 adolescent subjects (45 schizophrenia, 39 healthy). SHAP explainability was applied to identify and validate key biomarkers. The Random Forest achieved 90.48% subject-level accuracy (AUC=0.9339, sensitivity=95.56%), with second-order gamma-band scattering coefficients at electrode P3 emerging as the most discriminative features. No LLMs were involved; this is a signal-processing/traditional-ML study on a psychiatric EEG dataset.
missing_or_uncertain_fields: num_llms_assessed — no LLMs evaluated in this paper
llms_evaluated — no LLMs evaluated; study uses Random Forest and SVM only
